summary: False used Proposition3.14, a used source/sink mismatch, and a specified-class Lefschetz counterexample are demonstrated. A local folded-word mismatch is Minor. Main coordinate-ring falsity is not established; sufficient factorial and orientation repairs are verified within stated scope.

problems.title: Proposition 3.14 does not follow from coordinate-ring containment
problems.claim: Affine factorial irreducible X with an integral sink-recurrent seed on X and C[X] subset U has C[X]=A.
assumptions_checked: X=A1 times Gm smooth affine factorial irreducible
One mutable x and frozen invertible y
Rank-one graph has no arrows and is sink-recurrent
Standing special frozen row assumption also holds
R contained in each of the only two Laurent charts
problems.check: Exchange x*t=1+y; t=(1+y)/x has pole at x=0,y=1. Mutated torus map contracts t nonzero,y=-1 to one point.
problems.result: Proposition3.14 false; ring inclusion does not make mutated tori open immersions; codimension-one complement remains.
problems.counterevidence: Counterexample is not asserted to satisfy all of Theorem3.13's stronger deletion/contraction data. No main braid-theorem counterexample.
problems.impact: Theorem3.13 explicitly invokes false3.14 at its last step, a central induction dependency. Normal-only scope also lacks factoriality.
problems.correction: Add full rank, factoriality, regularity of all initial and one-step variables, frozen units and R subset U. Proof uses units/irreducibility/primality and principal-open tori covering codimension one. Adequate for actual factorial braid application with explicit preceding regularity argument and consistent orientation; normal-only generality unresolved.

independent_acceptance.hypotheses: Checked seed-on-X means an initial dense open torus only. X=A1 times Gm, one mutable x and frozen invertible y, exchange column (0,1), factoriality, sink recurrence, really full rank and special frozen row all hold.
independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: R=C[x,y,y^-1] lies in both Laurent charts because x=(1+y)/t, while t=(1+y)/x is not regular at (0,1). The mutated torus map collapses all (t,-1), t nonzero, and misses a codimension-one portion of x=0. Thus containment alone supplies neither the claimed open immersion nor the coordinate-ring equality.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Independently checked the strengthened criterion: full rank makes every exchange binomial a nonunit in the Laurent ring; Laurent factorization proves initial/adjacent irreducibility and their nonassociation; units are frozen Laurent monomials. Since R is contained in A=U and frozen units already lie in R, these facts descend to R. Factoriality makes the variables prime, and actual regular initial/adjacent variables give principal-open tori covering every height-one prime. Normality then gives R=U=A. The actual factorial braid application needs the stated regularity and consistent orientation; general normal-only Theorem 3.13 remains unresolved.
independent_acceptance.impact: The false proposition is explicitly used in the core induction. A verified stronger replacement is recorded separately; no main theorem counterexample is claimed.

problems.title: The leading induction vertex is a source under the printed graph convention
problems.claim: For beta=ii beta-prime, the leading mutable vertex meets the sink/incoming-neighbor criterion used in Theorem4.10.
assumptions_checked: SL2 typeA1 beta=1111 has Demazure w0
Half-root normalization fixed by later source formulas
problems.check: Delta0=x1,Delta1=x2,Delta2=x3,Delta3=1; omega=dlogx1 wedge dlogx2+dlogx2 wedge dlogx3; B23=1. Literal graph2→3, incoming neighbors of2 empty, contraction incorrectly retains mutable3.
problems.result: Used sink hypothesis and stated contraction identification fail under printed convention.
problems.counterevidence: Reversing graph convention gives correct neighbor set; exchange algebra is unchanged. Main theorem not refuted.
problems.impact: Explicit wrong mutable rank at a used central deletion/contraction induction step.
problems.correction: Reverse graph convention globally or consistently use source/outgoing recurrence and criterion; local exchange x2x2'=x1+x3 shows x3 is unit on divisor and must be frozen.

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: For A1 beta=1111 the distinguished and almost-positive sequences give frozen 1 and mutable 2,3. With the source's consistent half-root normalization, omega=dlog x1 wedge dlog x2+dlog x2 wedge dlog x3, hence B23=1. Under the explicit arrow convention vertex 2 is a source; freezing its incoming set leaves the wrong mutable rank. On x2=0 the exchange x2*x2'=x1+x3 makes x3 a unit, identifying the outgoing neighbor that must be frozen.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: A globally reversed graph convention or consistently source/outgoing formulation mirrors the recurrence without changing the symmetric exchange sum. This fixes the demonstrated local mismatch; it does not make the literal original invocation valid.
independent_acceptance.impact: Used central deletion/contraction condition fails; severity follows the derivation, while the coordinate-ring conclusion is not refuted.

problems.title: The specified Lefschetz class vanishes on an admissible two-dimensional torus
problems.claim: Every even-dimensional double braid variety satisfies the curious Lefschetz property with respect to [omega_beta] as defined with d=d(beta).
assumptions_checked: suffix121321 reduced w0 and Demazure product w0
J={1,2}; almost-positive initial values s1,s3, both frozen
problems.check: h2=1,h1=alpha3vee(t2),h0=alpha1vee(t1)alpha3vee(t2), a13=a31=0. All local wedge terms zero, hence omega=0. H0=H2=C while multiplication by omega is zero. Printed indexing also requires H0≅H4=0.
problems.result: Specified-class theorem false even after correcting dimension center; printed curious Poincare symmetry also has doubled center.
problems.counterevidence: Laurent coordinate ring and mixed Tate cohomology hold. Corrected-center Poincare symmetry is not refuted. Other form dlogt1 wedge dlogt2 works on this torus.
problems.impact: Material failure of an explicit cohomological application, not of main cluster-coordinate-ring identification.
problems.correction: Use full-dimension exponent D/2-p and target D-p+s when D even, but also require appropriate nondegenerate class or alter prescribed form. Only torus-specific alternative verified; no general replacement theorem asserted.

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: For SL4 and beta=13.121321 the suffix gives the reduced longest permutation, dimension is 8-6=2, and both solid indices are frozen. The source torus criterion gives (C*)^2. Lemma 2.8 gives h2=1, h1=alpha3vee(t2), h0=alpha1vee(t1)alpha3vee(t2). Orthogonality a13=a31=0 makes both possible wedge contributions zero, so omega=0. The printed index asks H0 to map isomorphically to H4=0; even after correcting to exponent D/2-p, multiplication by this zero class cannot identify nonzero H0 and H2.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The all-frozen Laurent coordinate ring and mixed Tate cohomology survive. A nonzero dlog t1 wedge dlog t2 repairs this particular torus only; no universal replacement class theorem is certified.
independent_acceptance.impact: An explicit cohomological guarantee fails beyond a typographical center error. Major applies to that guarantee, not to every cluster result.

problems.title: A G2 folded mutation word is not the projection of its listed lift
problems.claim: Table1(f)'s lifted orbit-mutation sequence lifts the corresponding Table1(b) folded sequence, as used in Corollary6.5.
assumptions_checked: Finite rational diagnostic has nonzero denominators
problems.check: Orbit projection of lift is (3,6,3). With B=[[0,-3],[1,0]], x3=2,x6=5, coefficients1, folded maps yield (11/5,28/5) and (7/5,52/25).
problems.result: Literal table projection and corresponding folding-map assertion disagree.
problems.counterevidence: Both orbit words palindromic, so reversing composition cannot resolve it. Listed lift passes independent braid comparison; no long-braid theorem refutation.
problems.impact: Local displayed sequence defect; central equivalence remains supported by corrected projection and valid listed lift.
problems.correction: Replace folded word in this row by(3,6,3).

independent_acceptance.decisive_reasoning: The orbit blocks {5,6,7} and {12} project the listed lift to (3,6,3). Both compared words are palindromes, so composition reversal cannot fix the mismatch. Direct rational mutation at (2,5) with B=[[0,-3],[1,0]] gives (11/5,28/5) and (7/5,52/25), with all denominators nonzero.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Changing this folded row to (3,6,3) restores the orbit projection. Existing exact restricted principal-coefficient comparison of the listed lift is retained as bounded counterevidence, not a new run or universal table certification.
independent_acceptance.impact: Local table transcription defect. The distinct all-solid G2 labeling concern remains Needs Evidence and is not promoted to an additional finding.
